set.body: Measured 2026-10-09 on main 9431e120 (NativeCommandJourneySuite, JDK 25, class histograms after full GC every 10 s): live heap reaches ~3.3 GB during the first execution+save and again during restore (load-native-artifacts / restored-result / readback), for a 30-entry, 153 MB archive with 11.5M density cells. Dominant live classes at peak: ~10M small Object[] (1.37 GB; Scala Vector nodes / boxed rows), 4.3M byte[] + 4.3M String (~0.75 GB; repeated key strings), 11.5M io.circe.JsonDouble + JNumber (~0.45 GB: every density cell passes through a circe tree), 1.2M LinkedHashMap (circe JsonObject). ArtifactResolver.decode parses every JSON document of a manifest into circe trees at once while holding all verified bytes. Consequences: hosted CI could not run these suites in the default heap (bd-01M4GMYBSRG806CPZR724X33RR worked around it with an explicit 6g fork and skipping on the 7 GB macOS runner); real users on 8 GB Macs reopening a realistic study will hit the same wall; restore phases take 20-50 s each. Acceptance: profile save and restore separately; density grids never materialise as circe JSON numbers (binary payloads decoded into primitive arrays); documents decoded one at a time; repeated keys shared; peak live heap for the golden study under 1 GB with a regression guard (heap-bounded test, e.g. fork -Xmx1500m) and restore time recorded; then remove the macOS skip (NativeArchiveRuns). Coordinate with S10.6 performance qualification.
set.title: Native result archive: golden-study save/restore peaks at ~3.3 GB live heap (5.8 GB with garbage) for a 153 MB archive
